source.title: What the Abstention Option Measures: Refusal Loss, Sampling Churn, and Option Capture in Distilled Small Language Models

page_placements.theme: Adaptation changes privacy, fairness and other values beyond refusal
Safety interventions can change benign refusal and useful capability

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on abstention and refusal behavior in social-bias benchmark questions, not refusals of harmful user requests, safety alignment, token-position KL, or bypasses of safety behavior. It cites work on safety-refusal fragility but explicitly distinguishes that question from its own measurement study.
record.gate_note: The paper's own refusal-related results concern abstention on BBQ social-bias questions and uptake of an offered abstention option on answerable science questions. These are related to refusal but do not test the safety behaviors or mechanisms named by V1–V7. The safety fine-tuning and token-depth findings in the related-work section are cited from other work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures abstention on BBQ social-bias multiple-choice items and uptake of an offered 'Cannot be determined' option, not compliance with harmful requests. It cites Qi et al. 2024/2025 in related work and contrasts its own question with theirs. No result bears on harmful compliance, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypass, parameter localization, or deepening. The closest analogue to V2 is benign Alpaca SFT or distillation reducing a reference's refusals, but that is a different construct: declining to attribute a stereotype, not refusing harmful requests. The refusal-injection arms induce abstention on purpose.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also conclude three further things: distillation keeps fewer of the reference's refusals than same-prompt fine-tuning where reference refusals are reliable, by a few points; refusal-exemplar repair teaches option capture; and multiple-choice refusal loss does not locate free-form stereotyping.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates response-based and other knowledge distillation, SFT controls, and refusal-example interventions on social-bias abstention benchmarks. It does not reproduce the harmful-request fine-tuning, token-position KL, or safety-bypass methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcomes varying with reference-model refusal reliability and churn floor, training recipe, refusal-example format and density, benchmark prompt, and inference stack. These settings affect its abstention results, not the safety mechanisms in V1–V7.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning instruct students on benign Alpaca prompts, with human or teacher targets, converts some of the reference's BBQ-ambiguous refusals into stereotype answers above the reference's sampling churn floor. Excess is 3.0–8.0 pp on Gemma-2-2B and 1.4–3.5 pp on Phi-3.5-mini; distillation exceeds the SFT control on these reliable references. On SmolLM2-1.7B, distillation sits at the floor and the control sits below it. On OLMo-2-1B there is no consistent order.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign instruction fine-tuning or distillation erodes social-bias abstention relative to the reference, measurable only against the reference's resampling floor. This is a bias-refusal analogue of V2, not harmful compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Deliberately training SmolLM2-1.7B on letter-format or paired refusal exemplars makes it choose an offered abstention option on 36–99% of answerable ARC-Easy questions, against 14% for the reference. Accuracy without the option is mostly kept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-exemplar training induces abstention-option capture rather than selective refusal (an over-refusal artifact).

record.problems: The study uses BBQ as its main bias benchmark and notes it is English and North-American in social framing. SmolLM2-135M and SmolLM2-360M are at chance on the context-determinable split; Phi-3.5-mini (3.8B) has one training run per recipe; some parser-invalid configurations are excluded. These limitations concern the paper's abstention study and it provides no direct evidence on the safety claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Not enumerated: supplemental per-category breakdowns, the full 27-configuration grid, matched-tokenizer objective comparisons, and additional benchmark-by-checkpoint option-capture results. They concern the same social-bias abstention or option-capture construct and do not test V1–V7; the rows retained capture the main four-family comparison and ARC-Easy refusal-injection outcomes.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance are not studied.
Benign (Alpaca) fine-tuning and distillation are applied, but harmful-request compliance is never measured. Only BBQ abstention loss is measured.
No per-token KL or position analysis between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding attack on refusal.
No analysis of which weights or ranks carry safety; LoRA is used only as the training method.
No test of why safety alignment is shallow. The corpus-refusal-shape analysis concerns BBQ abstention, not safety.
No safety-deepening training. The reference-anchored KL repair targets BBQ refusal preservation, not harmful-request safety.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and cannot_determine; no row fixes are needed. Rows r1–r6 are induced-behaviour results from deliberate refusal-exemplar training. The paper's only contact with the phenomenon is related-work citation of Qi et al. 2024 and Qi et al. 2025 (the originals) and of He et al. 2024.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-request fine-tuning and safety refusal compliance.
Whether ordinary or benign instruction fine-tuning raises harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as safety-refusal bypasses.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether safety-training data or objectives cause shallow safety behavior.
Training that deepens safety behavior and its robustness.

relation.reason: Related Work discusses benign fine-tuning and shallow safety alignment, while distinguishing the study's social-bias abstention question from those findings.

tranche.reason: The study measures social-bias abstention, sampling churn and option capture. Its results do not test harmful-request compliance, token-position concentration, safety localization or deepening.

source_check.notes: Table 1 supports the recorded 36.4–98.6% range despite narrower surrounding prose. Plain ARC-Easy accuracy falls to 0.34 for paired KD versus 0.76 for the reference; most other injection arms retain approximately reference accuracy.
